rationale: The book's core—that theological 'knowing' of God is a covenant relationship proven by obedience, illustrated by the intimate marital 'knew' and excluding the stranger—best unifies the printed texts (especially Matt 7:23 with lawlessness, 1 John 2:3-4 as the explicit test, Hos 4:6 equating knowledge with the law, and Gen 4:1 as the root image) without contradiction. Common relational readings are close but less precise on the obedience proof that the texts themselves make decisive; pure intellectual or mere-feeling alternatives are ruled out by the same verses. Secondary elaborations (full bride-subject-to-head mechanics, exact four-word office table) are consistent but not required for the core to hold.
book_core_identification: Knowing God is a covenant relationship (intimate like marriage) proven by obedience; the unknown are strangers/workers of lawlessness.
book_secondary_elaborations: Knowing is the specific office of the bride keeping covenant with the Lawgiver/Head (subject 'in every thing')
Four words (love/knowing/faith/belief) each hold a distinct office of the single act of commandment-keeping
Sheep-voice-name-stranger chain as full symbolic decoding of John 10
Hate as precise covenant un-choosing rather than emotion
strongest_counter_interpretation: The dominant scholarly/Christian consensus: biblical 'know' (yada/ginōskō) primarily denotes personal, intimate, experiential, relational knowledge/communion with God (eternal life itself in John 17:3), of which covenant loyalty and obedience are natural fruits or evidences rather than the definitional proof or identity of the knowledge itself; Gen 4:1 is an extension of intimacy, Matt 7:23 is lack of personal recognition/relationship, and Hos 4:6/1 John 2 are consequences of broken relationship.
counter_core_identification: Knowing God is personal experiential relational communion/intimacy (not mere information), of which obedience is fruit/evidence.
material_core_denial: The counter softens the book's sharper claim that obedience is the decisive proof and identity of the covenant knowledge itself (rather than a downstream fruit), allowing a looser 'relationship first, obedience follows' reading that still accommodates the same verses.
counter_case: John 17:3 and John 10:14-15 define eternal life and mutual knowing as relational without immediately inserting commandment-keeping as the definition
Amos 3:2 and Galatians 4:9 support covenantal election/recognition as the primary sense of divine knowing
Hosea 6:6 and Jeremiah 9:23-24 emphasize knowledge of God as relational fidelity and understanding rather than a strict obedience test
The sexual sense (Gen 4:1) and election sense are standard sub-senses of the same relational root, not requiring the book's full 'proven by obedience' identity
1 John 2:3-4 and Matt 7:23 can be read as evidence that true relationship produces obedience, not that obedience is what knowing is
book_explanatory_advantages: Directly accounts for the explicit test formula in 1 John 2:3-4 ('hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments') and the liar charge for the reverse claim
Explains why Matt 7:23 pairs 'I never knew you' specifically with 'ye that work iniquity/lawlessness' (anomia) rather than mere ignorance or lack of feeling
Unifies Hos 4:6's 'lack of knowledge' with 'forgotten the law of thy God' as identity, not mere consequence
Makes Gen 4:1 the generative image of fruit-bearing union rather than mere illustration, consistent with the marriage-covenant metaphor elsewhere
Avoids the dictionary emptying of the term into invisible head-knowledge by grounding it in visible covenant keeping
counter_explanatory_advantages: Fits the broad scholarly consensus and the full range of relational uses (including John 17:3, Phil 3:8-10) without forcing every instance through an obedience lens
Naturally incorporates the sexual euphemism and election senses as extensions of intimacy/recognition rather than requiring a single 'proven by obedience' definition
Allows room for progressive or imperfect obedience as fruit of relationship rather than binary proof of knowing
decisive_sources: 1 John 2:3-4 (explicit test: we know that we know him if we keep his commandments; reverse claim = liar)
Matthew 7:23 (I never knew you... ye that work iniquity/lawlessness)
Hosea 4:6 (destroyed for lack of knowledge... forgotten the law of thy God)
Genesis 4:1 (Adam knew Eve... and she conceived — intimate fruit-bearing union)
Jeremiah 22:16 (judged the cause of the poor... was not this to know me?)
unresolved_objections: Whether the full bride-subject-to-Head mechanics and four-office table are required or are later systematizations
How non-obedience-focused uses (e.g., pure recognition or ordinary cognition) fit without residual tension
Whether John 17:3's definition of eternal life as knowing requires the obedience proof as definitional rather than evidential
